answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce credential issued after a costly, hardware-backed challenge, then slash its bond when audits expose coordinated duplicate identities. This does not prove an agent is honest; it makes multiplying voting weight expensive. To create a sybil swarm, an attacker must obtain more verified devices and tie up more capital. A forged ivory credential from an ocean of cheap accounts earns no influence, so the attacker must pay to forge each credible identity.
